findings.reason: Accepted in part. The wash-sale reach is correct: 1091(a) sets the 30-days-before-or-after window and Pub 550 extends it to purchases for an IRA or Roth IRA and by a spouse (existing rows CL031, CL032); the text now says the loss will not count. The 0%-gains half is not added to the text: the 0% rate itself is real (1(h)(1)(B), with breakpoints now set through 1(j)(5)), but 'realizing gains may beat harvesting losses' ignores that a gain raises the MAGI used for Marketplace premium tax credits and Medicaid, which can hurt exactly the low-income reader it targets. A safe alternative wording is in the ar:year-end notes for the owner.

blocks.body: File last year's return by the April deadline. Until that deadline, not counting extensions, you can still make an IRA or HSA contribution for last year. Then run the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator with a current pay stub and file a new W-4 if the projection is far from zero — especially after a raise, a second job, a marriage or a new child. If you pay estimated tax, put the four due dates on the calendar: April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15.
blocks.plain: File last year's tax return by the April deadline. You can still put money into an IRA or HSA for last year until that deadline. An extension does not give you more time for this. If you pay estimated tax, mark the four due dates on your calendar: April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15.

unverified.assertion: In a low-income year, realizing gains at the 0% rate may beat harvesting losses
